guideline: Annotation guidelines specify evaluation options (e.g., 'equally correct/better/worse/wrong' for definitions; 'good/bad/borderline' for explanations; 'yes/yes but same pattern/no/borderline' for examples)

Annotators evaluate generated definitions, free-form explanations, and example sentences using predefined categories (e.g., equally correct/better/worse/wrong for definitions; good/bad/borderline for explanations; yes/yes but same pattern/no/borderline for examples).

For the dictionary-style definition generation task we ask the annotator to tag the definitions provided by the two LLMs in comparison with the WordNet definitions as selected in the gold standard dataset. For each item, the annotator has four options: equally correct, better than gold, worse than gold, wrong. In the free explanation task the annotator has to evaluate the quality of the unconstrained explanation produced by the models for the target word in context. The evaluation options include good, bad and borderline. In the example generation task the annotator has to assess the ability of the LLMs to generate three distinct sentences that use the target word in the same sense as in the sentence under examination. In this case four options could be selected: yes (all three sentences are accurate), yes but same pattern, no (at least one sentence is clearly incorrect), and borderline
